title: Bhishma's fall
hook: losing every day to their own grandsire, the Pandavas walk across the field at night to ask him how he can be killed

segments.voice: Your line yesterday was to be killed by you would be an honor. Twice Krishna leapt from the chariot and ran at him, and twice Arjuna pulled him back. And the old man is still standing. Day eight hundred twenty-seven.

Night, and the Pandava camp is quiet in the wrong way. Another day has gone to Bhishma. He is the commander of the other side, and he is also the elder these brothers grew up calling grandsire. Yudhishthira can't see a way through. Then he remembers the first morning, when he walked over to Bhishma unarmed. Bhishma told him then that he could not fight for the Pandavas but would still give them counsel, and that the question of how he could be beaten should be asked again another time. So the brothers set their weapons aside, and with Krishna they walk across the dark field to the enemy's tent. Today, the brothers ask it.
screen: `ANOTHER DAY LOST TO BHISHMA.` → `A PROMISE OF COUNSEL.` → `ACROSS THE FIELD AT NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Bhishma doesn't reach for a sword. In Ganguli's English, he welcomes them, asks why they've come, and offers to do whatever he can for them. Yudhishthira asks the question out loud. How can you be defeated? How can we win, when you stand in the way? It's an unbearable thing to ask a man you love. And Bhishma answers it. As long as he holds his bow, he says, no one can bring him down. But there is a warrior he will not fight. Shikhandi, Drupada's son, was born a daughter, and Bhishma has vowed never to raise a weapon against one he counts as a woman. Put Shikhandi in front, he tells them. Let Arjuna shoot from behind. Then the brothers walk back across the field, and the text lets us hear Arjuna come apart. He remembers being a small boy, climbing into Bhishma's lap, getting dust on his clothes, and calling him father. And Bhishma gently correcting him: not your father, child, your father's father. How can I kill him, Arjuna asks. Krishna steadies him. Arjuna has already promised to fight, and Bhishma himself has told them the way. Hold the scene for a moment. The enemy commander is also the family elder. He tells the truth even when the truth is his own death. And the grandson who must aim at him once sat in his lap. The text doesn't make any of it easy.
screen: `THE ENEMY WELCOMES THEM` · `"HOW CAN YOU BE DEFEATED?"` · `SHIKHANDI IN FRONT` · then, large: `A BOY IN HIS GRANDSIRE'S LAP`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let your hands rest. Bring to mind one person whose counsel you would trust even when it's hard to hear. A teacher, an elder, an old friend. Breathing in, see their face. Breathing out, quietly name one question you would bring them, the way the brothers brought theirs across the field. You don't need their answer today. Just let the question be asked. If you pray, you can bring that question into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's fall. Tonight it begins with a question asked in his own tent, and an honest answer that he gives against himself.
Your line: put Shikhandi in front. Today, if someone asks you a hard question, try giving the honest answer, even when it costs you a little. Day eight hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: Retellings of the Mahabharata keep the night when the Pandavas visit Bhishma's tent and he tells them how he can be overcome.

match.prompt: who did what that night — tap the pairs.
pairs: asked how Bhishma could be defeated
told them the way, against himself

myth: the Pandavas went to Bhishma's tent to attack him in the dark
they set their weapons aside and went to ask his counsel.
Bhishma had promised counsel even though he fought for the other side
that promise is why Yudhishthira dares to ask.
Arjuna heard Bhishma's answer with relief
he grieves on the way back, remembering calling Bhishma father as a child.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. your own grandsire is destroying your army day after day. what do you do?
options: attack his tent under cover of night.
walk to his tent unarmed and ask him how he can be beaten.
ask Krishna to break his word and fight Bhishma himself.
fork.reveal: Yudhishthira goes and asks, and Bhishma, true to his promise of counsel, tells him: put Shikhandi in front.

original.note: Drupada's child, born a daughter and raised as a son; the warrior Bhishma will not fight.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas found Bhishma's weak spot.
what it means: Bhishma gave them his weak spot himself, because he'd promised counsel and wouldn't lie.
what a scholar hears: the scene sets duty against love on both sides: Bhishma's honesty kills him, and Arjuna's promise to fight makes him the one who must do it.
recall: dark, in red, with a noose

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Bhishma-vadha Parva), the Pandavas' night visit to Bhishma and Arjuna's grief

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that the brothers lay aside armor and weapons for the visit, that Krishna goes with them, and that Bhishma's counsel names Shikhandi with Arjuna behind him.

Confirm Arjuna's memory (climbing into Bhishma's lap as a child, calling him father, Bhishma replying he is his father's father) and the wording 'one he counts as a woman' for Bhishma's vow regarding Shikhandi.
Bhishma is called grandsire throughout; he is strictly the Pandavas' great-uncle.
Days 825 and 826 were not on disk while writing; the review is generic. Check it doesn't repeat their angle.

Editor: hook now ties the promise of counsel to the first-morning scene of day 824 (ask me again another time) instead of 'before the war'; cut the superlatives 'strangest meeting of the war' and 'loved him most'; 'born a woman' now 'born a daughter'; practice changed from love-and-disagreement (too close to day 824's someone-at-odds) to a trusted counselor; howItsDone no longer claims 'many tellings' and television.
Original word शिखण्डी: confirm Devanagari form and pronunciation.
